Support useSystemPicker on Linux (Wayland/Pipewire)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

On Linux with Pipewire, session.setDisplayMediaRequestHandler({ useSystemPicker: true }) does not use the system screen-picker.

With Pipewire it doesn't make sense to use a custom handler, because it always returns only one source and breaks many different electron based apps that provide custom pickers (e. g: element)

### Proposed Solution

The behavior that is implemented for macOS with useSystemPicker: true should also work under Linux with Wayland.

### Alternatives Considered

Custom code in Electron apps, that detects Wayland and then always picks the first source automatically.

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: macOS: dialog.showOpenDialog fails to show custom macOS packages (LSTypeIsPackage) when filtered by extension in Electron 36.2.0+ (worked in 35.7.5; 36.0.0 showed all files)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

36.2.0+ (including latest)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

15.5 (Sequoia)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

35.7.5

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When using dialog.showOpenDialog() with filters: [{ name: 'rich text files', extensions: ['rtf', 'rtfd'] }], the open panel should show and allow selection of custom macOS bundles registered by the an (e.g., .rtf registered by Text Edit) where the document type has LSTypeIsPackage = true.

### Actual Behavior

•	36.0.0: filters are ignored — all files are visible/selectable. (Matches issue #46883.)
•	36.2.0+ (36.2.0, 36.7.x): no files are selectable for custom bundles; the panel shows zero matching items for .rtf/.rtfd, even though these bundles exist in the folder and are recognized by Finder. Interestingly, .app bundles can be filtered/shown (likely due to the fix in PR #47825 for app → modern bundle UTType mapping).


### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/3afd1a232bdd7c2595ddb2cc885dcc98

### Additional Information

You'll need to create a .rtf file using Text Edit. From the "Format" menu, select "Rich Text" and save the file.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Opening dev tools should not produce any ERROR messages.

### Actual Behavior

Whenever the dev tools are opened two errors are printed by the main process:

```
[main] [43463:0827/061952.334107:ERROR:CONSOLE:1] "Request Autofill.enable failed. {"code":-32601,"message":"'Autofill.enable' wasn't found"}", source: devtools://devtools/bundled/core/protocol_client/protocol_client.js (1)
[main] [43463:0827/061952.334143:ERROR:CONSOLE:1] "Request Autofill.setAddresses failed. {"code":-32601,"message":"'Autofill.setAddresses' wasn't found"}", source: devtools://devtools/bundled/core/protocol_client/protocol_client.js (1)
```

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/CodeBishop/d48f16abcf5275e1ebaba83e346f98d1

### Additional Information

You know that thing where you're in a dev meeting with 20 other devs and a security inspection team and every time you open the dev tools it prints out two errors and you say "don't worry boss, those are normal ERROR messages and not related to the problem we're talking about" and your boss says "it's all good, no one here is worried about seeing ERROR messages appear in our critical infrastructure software!"

Ha ha, yeah, it turns out that's actually NOT how your boss handles it...

nodes.title: Expose FFmpeg bindings
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Chromium bundles FFmpeg, so it is shipped in Electron as well.

It would be great to have Electron expose a module with bindings to this bundled FFmpeg.

### Proposed Solution

Create a module that exposes bindings to FFmpeg from the main process.

### Alternatives Considered

Installing a third-party node bindings module dependency, but it is not as reliable as binding directly to the bundled FFmpeg from Electron. There may be incompatibilities caused by the FFmpeg version, and the binary may not be found at the expected locations. By bundling directly to Electron, both problems can be avoided, and the exposed bindings can match the FFmpeg API exactly.

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: Fresh Electron launch eats first ON-CLICK event (windows)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.3.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

windows 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

I expect a newly created Electron window (on windows/linux) to accept and process ON-CLICK events immediately, whether it is focused or not. 

### Actual Behavior

* The "first ON-CLICK on an electron window after launch" is eaten and does not reach the content DOM. 
* Curiously, this happens even if you reisize the window first (Which makes the window active). 
* Curiously, ON-MOUSEDOWN works fine.
* Curiously, CSS click animation is still triggered on a clicked element, the ON-CLICK event is just not delivered

Reproduction steps:

Start electron container with a button that has an ON-CLICK handler, from a fresh start, try each of these actions:

1. immediately click on button without focusing window -> ON-CLICK handler not fired (expected it to fire)
2. resize window first then click on button -> ON-CLICK handler not fired (expected it to fire)
3. click anywhere on window first, then click on button -> ON-CLICK handler fires


### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

I foud some bugs and mentions talking about behavior like this as it relates to the Mac, and complying with (or not complying with) Mac's "first click focuses" behavior when the window is inactive.. 

I want to be clear **this is NOT occuring every time the Electron window becomes inactive**.. only on the **VERY FIRST ON-CLICK after launch**, and also this is on windows, not the mac. It also does not affect ON-MOUSEDOWN, only ON-CLICK.

https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/212

I've tried "Fixes" for electron eating first clicks, includign using the mac-only (acceptFirstMouse: true) which does nothing, and I've tried:

```app.commandLine.appendSwitch('disable-features', 'FirstMouseClickActivatesWindow');
app.commandLine.appendSwitch('enable-features', 'AlwaysConsumeMouseEvents');
```

I can't find anything to get Electron to stop eating the very first click after launch....

However, this is not on the mac. I've tried all the "Fixes" I can find for this.. includign using the mac-only (acceptFirstMouse: true) which does nothing. I've tried:

```app.commandLine.appendSwitch('disable-features', 'FirstMouseClickActivatesWindow');
app.commandLine.appendSwitch('enable-features', 'AlwaysConsumeMouseEvents');
```

I can't find anything to get Electron to stop eating the very first click after launch.

nodes.title: Playwright browser launched inside utilityProcess has no Internet connectivity
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

When attempting to launch a Playwright-controlled browser inside an Electron utilityProcess, the browser cannot access the Internet.

The same Playwright code works correctly when run in the main process or in a regular Node.js child process before packaging.

However, after packaging the Electron application, using child_process.fork() becomes very problematic (due to ASAR restrictions, lack of proper Node runtime, etc.).

utilityProcess seems like a good replacement for child_process.fork() because it works after packaging, but when running Playwright in it, the launched browser has no network access.

This makes it impossible to run Playwright in a packaged Electron app.

### Proposed Solution

Allow utilityProcess to support full networking capabilities so that processes launched from it can open TCP/UDP sockets and child processes (like Playwright browsers) without restrictions.

Ideally, provide an explicit option (similar to allowNetworking or equivalent) when calling utilityProcess.fork().

Ensure that browsers or other processes launched from inside utilityProcess inherit the necessary permissions to access the Internet.

### Alternatives Considered

...

### Additional Information

Electron version: [37.2.3]

Playwright version: [1.54.2]

OS: [Windows]

Expected behavior: Playwright browser launched inside utilityProcess should have Internet connectivity like it does in main process.

### Problem Description

It would be great to add context menu items for copying and saving video frames in Electron applications. The Electron API currently does not directly support this feature.
The Chromium team implemented the functionality to copy/save video frames in 2023, with the relevant MR being: [chormium mr link](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/4550250). It is hoped that this feature can be synchronized to Electron for implementation.

### Proposed Solution

Electron's WebFrameMain API is a JavaScript abstraction of RenderFrameHost. Same like using `copyImageAt` method,  exposing copyVideoFrameAt and saveVideoFrameAs Method on Electron was a Feasible approaches.

### Alternatives Considered

none

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: Electron app loses its snapped state when restored from minimized in Windows 11
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.

### Electron Version

37.1.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro, version 24H2, OS build 26100

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

1. Snap the Electron app window to one side of the screen.  
2. Minimize the window.  
3. Restore it from the taskbar.  
4. The Electron window should stay snapped after being restored. (On Windows 11, snapped windows have sharp corners on all four edges.)

### Actual Behavior

When restoring the Electron window, the snapped state is lost. On Windows 11, the window corners change from sharp (snapped) to rounded (unsnapped).  


### Testcase Gist URL

[default fiddle app](https://gist.github.com/arshcaria/d1fe4241fc887c57aa65d5edae9b5dc2)

### Additional Information


- This issue was previously reported in https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/31451 (now closed)
- @codebytere mentioned that the issue was fixed, but the commit appears to address a different problem. The snapped state is still lost when minimizing and restoring the window on Windows 11.
